A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Animate-X research work, with 25 readable pages including Appendices A–E. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the scientific content is identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original animation experiments on A2Bench, TikTok and Fashion, a user study, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, user-study outcomes and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix A retain identical Animate-X architecture, implicit and explicit Pose Indicators, pose transformations, and training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: The collected human training videos, TikTok, Fashion and A2Bench coverage are unchanged, as are the self-driven, rescaled-pose and other demonstrated animation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding quantitative and qualitative comparison, including Tables 1–3 and 7–8. No baseline is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings, metrics and sample sizes are identical, including the 10 TikTok, 100 Fashion and 100 A2Bench evaluation videos and the 10-participant user study.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D retain the same component ablations, IPI-weight and pose-transformation sensitivity analyses, robustness examples and qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions use identical point-estimate and user-preference reporting. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8, plotted results and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Animate-X's A2Bench FVD remains 703.87 under the rescaled-pose setting in Table 1.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, training loss, attention expressions and mathematical descriptions are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about universal character animation, the Pose Indicator, A2Bench and comparative performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of IPI/EPI and pose-alignment tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning hands, faces and real-time generation, together with the same ethical discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including Appendix A's hardware, resolution, frame count, optimizer, learning rates and sampling settings. Benchmark construction details and access links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and statements positioning Animate-X relative to prior work are identical.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to 'Preprint. Technical Report.' The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 14 October 2024 to v2 dated 11 December 2024. All body wording and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All 15 figures and eight tables retain identical captions, formatting and placement. Rendered pages differ only in the header wording and first-page arXiv stamp; the body layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The only differences are the publication-status header and arXiv version/date stamp. Methods, evidence, explanations, limitations and presentation of scientific content remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
